candidate.educational_objective: Recognize a serum sodium of 122 mmol/L as hyponatremia that warrants further assessment, including evaluation for neurologic manifestations and acuity of onset.

options.D: A mildly high value with no need for follow-up

candidate.rationale: Mayo Clinic Laboratories lists a serum sodium reference interval of 135-145 mmol/L for patients age 1 year and older. A sodium of 122 mmol/L is therefore hyponatremia. Hyponatremia can cause neurologic manifestations because of brain swelling, and clinical severity depends importantly on the rate of sodium decline as well as the absolute concentration.
candidate.source_claim_supported: The reference interval for serum sodium is 135-145 mmol/L for age 1 year and older; hyponatremia can produce neurologic manifestations and severity depends substantially on the rate of change.
candidate.stem: An adult client's serum sodium is 122 mmol/L. How should the nurse interpret this result?

warning: Technical candidate selection only. This file is not clinical audit evidence and does not establish PASS or FAIL.
